# Overview

This report applies the data-analysis methods from Module 08 to Case 31, Employees Federal Credit Union. The purpose is to connect each research question or hypothesis to its constructs, operationalization, measurement scale, and appropriate statistical test.

# Research Questions and Hypotheses

## Research Questions

- **R1:** Why do people join the Credit Union?
- **R2:** Why do members use other financial institutions when they need to borrow funds?
- **R3:** What are members’ attitudes and beliefs about the proficiency of credit union employees?
- **R4:** Are there perceived differences in employee proficiency, awareness of services, and operational effectiveness between members who live near the firm’s headquarters and members who live elsewhere?
- **R5:** How well are members aware of the services offered by the credit union?
- **R6:** What are members’ attitudes and beliefs about how effectively the credit union is operated?

## Hypotheses

- **H1:** Members’ awareness of regular share accounts will influence their opinions about how well the current financial services provided by the credit union meet their needs.
- **H2:** Members will not differ in their opinions of the credit union’s loan rate and the degree to which they agree that the credit union’s loan rate is lower than competitors.

# Method Justifications

## R1 and R2

R1 and R2 are descriptive research questions. The purpose is to identify the most common reasons members join the Credit Union or use other financial institutions when borrowing. Frequencies and percentages are appropriate because the questions focus on the distribution of response categories rather than testing a causal relationship.

If the response format uses a numeric rating scale, means and standard deviations may also be reported. A one-sample t-test should only be used when the item has a meaningful midpoint and the research question requires comparison with that midpoint.

## R3

R3 evaluates members’ perceptions of employee proficiency. Items `q3:q6` are treated as candidate indicators of one underlying construct. Cronbach’s alpha will evaluate internal consistency, while a one-factor analysis will provide initial evidence about whether the items measure one common dimension.

An employee proficiency index will be created only if the items show acceptable reliability, reasonable item-total correlations, suitable factor loadings, and consistent wording. If these conditions are not met, the items will be analyzed separately.

## R4

R4 compares members who live near the Credit Union’s headquarters with members who live elsewhere. Residence is the independent variable, and employee proficiency, service awareness, and operational effectiveness are the dependent outcomes.

An independent-samples t-test is appropriate for comparing the means of an interval-scale outcome across two residence groups. Chi-square tests are appropriate for categorical awareness/use variables because they compare the distribution of categories across the residence groups.

## R5

R5 asks how aware members are of the Credit Union’s services. Because each item refers to a different service, the awareness items should be summarized separately using frequencies and percentages. Combining the items into one average would make the resulting score difficult to interpret because awareness of one service is not necessarily equivalent to awareness of another service.

## R6

R6 evaluates members’ attitudes about operational effectiveness. The candidate items should first be reviewed for wording, measurement scale, and direction. Reverse-coded items should be aligned so that higher values represent more favorable evaluations.

Reliability analysis and one-factor analysis should be used before creating an operational effectiveness index. If the items do not form a coherent measure, they should remain separate and be analyzed individually.

## H1

H1 evaluates whether awareness of regular share accounts is associated with members’ perceptions of how well the Credit Union’s services meet their needs. Because awareness is ordinal, Spearman correlation is a reasonable initial method. Ordinal regression may also be appropriate if the outcome is ordinal and the group wants to model the relationship while controlling for other variables.

If the service-satisfaction measure is treated as approximately interval, the team may use correlation or simple linear regression. The choice should be justified by the response scale and measurement assumptions.

## H2

H2 compares two ratings provided by the same members: their opinion of the Credit Union’s loan rate and their agreement that the Credit Union’s loan rate is lower than competitors. A paired-samples t-test is appropriate because the observations are matched within respondents.

The analysis should report the mean and standard deviation for each item, the mean difference, the confidence interval, and the p-value. The interpretation should focus on whether the two related ratings differ meaningfully.

# Analysis Limitations

The proposed analyses depend on the quality and coding of the Case 31 data. Measurement scales should be verified against the questionnaire before analysis. Ordinal items may not fully satisfy interval-scale assumptions, and sample sizes may differ because of missing responses.

The research questions are primarily descriptive and comparative. The proposed tests can identify associations and group differences, but they cannot establish causation. Any composite index should be created only when statistical evidence and item wording support the decision.
